comment:
On behalf of the Sacramento River Source Water Protection Program (SRSWPP), thank you for the opportunity to review and comment on the Proposed Interim Registration Review Decision (“PID”) for carbaryl. The City of Sacramento, City of West Sacramento, and Sacramento County Water Agency sponsor the SRSWPP; this program is coordinated with other agencies that draw drinking water from the Sacramento River, including the East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD), and the Woodland-Davis Clean Water Agency.
The SRSWPP seeks to maintain the high quality of the Sacramento River drinking water supply. It is our responsibility as water utilities to ensure that the water we deliver to over 2 million customers is both healthful and aesthetically pleasing. Because our water supply intakes are downstream of an important agricultural region, our source water protection efforts include tracking USEPA regulatory notices regarding pesticides used in that region, and coordinating with growers and pesticide regulators on actions to facilitate protection of surface water.
In conjunction with our review of the Carbaryl PID, we also reviewed EPA’s recently released Draft Evaluation Supporting Proposed Mitigations Predicted to Avoid Jeopardy and Adverse Modification of Designated Critical Habitat and Reduce Take for Four Federally Listed Endangered and Threatened Species (“BE Memo”) , concerning the proposed mitigations that would apply to agricultural uses of carbaryl.
Contamination of drinking water sources from agricultural applications of carbaryl is possible in the Sacramento River Watershed downstream of agricultural land uses, as noted in the Revised Draft Human Health Risk Assessment (HHRA) for carbaryl :
Humans may be exposed to carbaryl in food and drinking water, since carbaryl may be applied directly to growing crops and application may result in carbaryl reaching surface and ground water sources of drinking water. [HHRA, p. 7]
Furthermore, carbaryl has been identified as a likely carcinogen, per the HHRA:
The Cancer Assessment Review Committee (CARC) classified carbaryl as “Likely to be Carcinogenic to Humans” [HHRA, p. 8]
While EPA’s risk assessment modeling concluded that agricultural use of carbaryl does not present a dietary cancer risk to adult subpopulations, the calculated cancer risk is greater than 1X10-6 and therefore not negligible:
The cancer (food and water) risk for adults 20-49 and adults 50-99 population subgroups is 2E-06, with water accounting for 89% of the total exposure. The cancer assessment included the EDWC provided by EFED resulting from application to almond (maximum labeled rate; 0.0972 ppm) as it provided the highest drinking water concentration. [HHRA, p. 10]
SRSWPP appreciates EPA’s inclusion of the primary carbaryl degradate 1-naphthol as a residue of concern in the dietary/drinking water cancer risk assessment, “as it was identified at significant concentration in the PDP monitoring program, is a significant environmental degradate, and is a significant metabolite in rat metabolism studies” [HHRA, p. 49].
Because of the potential risk to surface water drinking water sources within the Sacramento River Watershed, we support the proposed mitigations for agricultural uses of carbaryl as outlined in the Carbaryl PID and the associated BE Memo, specifically the following (item numbers are as shown in the Carbaryl PID, section IV A. Proposed Risk Mitigation and Regulatory Rationale, pp. 39-61):
1. Use Deletions: specifically, the proposed elimination of the use on rice
2. Rate Reductions: the proposed application rate reductions for sweet corn and turf
5. Rate Reductions…for Citrus: the proposed reduced application rate for citrus
9. Spray Drift Management measures, including limits on wind speed and inclusion of buffer zones for aquatic habitats
11. General Environmental Protection Measures, including Proposed Statements for Outdoor Label Consistency, Proposed Addition of General Outdoor Application Statements, Proposed Water Protection Statements, and Proposed Rain-Related Statements
If you have any questions on the preceding comments, please do not hesitate to contact me at (916) 808-1449. Thank you for the opportunity to review and comment on the Proposed Interim Registration Review Decision for carbaryl.
title: Comment submitted by Sacramento River Source Water Protection Program (SRSWPP)
